text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Tuesday.

LONDON - The UK's FTSE 100 index fell over one percent, dragged down by the prospect of an interest rate rise later this week and inflation figures which did little to calm fears that more rate rises may be needed to cool buoyant consumer demand. The FTSE 100 closed at 4,758.5, down 52.2 points, or 1.09 percent.

FRANKFURT - Shares forged ahead as the firm dollar lifted the blue chip DAX index to its sixth record close in a row. The DAX-30 index closed at 4,006.40, up 33.56 points, or 0.84 percent. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index ended at 4,030.10, up 26.75 points, or 0.67 percent.

PARIS - Shares fell, weighed down by profit taking and concerns about a sharp fall in London equities on fears of higher British interest rates. The CAC-40 index closed at 2,929.81, down 17.85 points, or 0.61 percent.

ZURICH - Shares jumped more than one percent to end above the psychologically important level of 6,000 points in the Swiss Market Index (SMI) for the first time. The Swiss market index closed at 6,012.6, up 65.6 points, or 1.10 percent.

MILAN - Shares closed mixed with telecoms mostly in retreat as investors took profits but selected banks were in strong demand, led by San Paolo and Banco di Napoli. The All Share Mibtel index closed at 13,774, down 30 points, or 0.22 percent.

AMSTERDAM - Shares ended slightly lower despite the market rallying early behind news that financial giant ING Groep had agreed its biggest ever purchase, a $2.2. billion buy of U.S. insurer Equitable Iowa. The AEX index closed at 918.04, down 0.81 points, or 0.09 percent.

TOKYO - Stocks broke their three-day losing streak, ending higher as the yen's decline against the dollar triggered bargain-hunting of blue-chip issues, brokers said. The 225-share Nikkei average closed at 19,853.89, up 148.72 points, or 0.75 percent.

HONG KONG - Stocks closed weaker due to nervousness over the outlook for other Asian markets and uncertainty over the local government's future land supply policy, but brokers said the downside was limited. The Hang Seng index closed at 14,792.17, down 66.41 points, or 0.45 percent.

SYDNEY - Tumbling gold stocks set off a 1.25 percent share market fall, which some dealers said could be the start of a downward correction from an 18 percent rally over the past three months. The All Ordinaries index closed at 2,679.2, down 33.8 points, or 1.25 percent.

JOHANNESBURG - Shares recovered early losses and ended in positive territory as golds launched a mini-rally to claw back some of Monday's steep fall, dealers said. The All-share index closed at 7,310.3, up 17.1 points, or 0.23 percent. The All Gold index closed at 923.7, up 19.8 points, or 0.27 percent, while the Industrial index closed at 8,766.3, up 23.3 points, or 2.19 percent.
